text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.

- Centre Party council encouraged its Euro-parliamentarians to pursue constructive policy of cooperation in European parliament, but voiced oppostion to third phase of monetary union and called for an advisory referendum on EMU.
- Baltic Sea region needs new security concept encompassing prevention of international crime and social disintegration as well as environmental protection, says Finnish MP Kimmo Kiljunen.
- Finnish men's team won World Cup cross-country skiing relay event at Kiruna in Sweden on Sunday.

- Value of Central Union of Agricultural Producers' share portfolio has tripled in less than four years, rising to about 300 million. Most of the gains have come from big holdings in food groups Raisio and Cultor.
- Poll of some 1,500 business leaders and politicians in Europe shows that Finland is expected to be among the first countries to join European Economic and Monetary Union.
- Polish Prime Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz, on official visit to Finland, sees prospects for Finnish and Polish businesses to cooperate in St Petersburg area.
- Lock maker Assa Abloy a "gold mine" for Finnish Metra, which holds 38 percent of Assa votes.
- UPM-Kymmene to invest 180 million markka to rebuild adhesive label machine at Jamsankoski in 1998.
- Most seats in local government sub-committees are held by men, contrary to the legal requirement that neither sex should occupy more than 40 percent of committee seats.
- Finnish banks have begun charging customers even for self-service bill payments on automatic teller machines.
- Thousands of Turku residents lit candles as Turku declared itself "Finland's Christmas city."
